podcast.title: Breakup and Reunion
podcast.body: K's Choice experienced a breakup in 2003, but later reunited in 2009. They have released more albums since their reunion, but none have achieved the same level of success as their hit song "Not An Addict." "There were more albums, followed by a breakup in 2003."

podcast.title: Continued Presence in Benelux
podcast.body: K's Choice maintains a significant presence in Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg, contrasting with their limited recognition in the rest of the world. "They continue to have a significant presence in Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg, but for the rest of the world, not so much."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of All Time: Part 2 (40-31)

podcast.title: Origin of Band Name
podcast.body: K's Choice was originally called "Just The Choice" but was forced to change their name to "K's Choice" at the last minute before their debut album's release due to an American band having prior claim to the name. They initially offered a cover story that "K" stood for Joseph K., the main character in Franz Kafka's novel *The Trial*, but later confessed the name change was simply because "K's Choice just sounded good." "It had to be changed to Case Choice at the very last second because an American band had dibs on the name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sam Bettens' Transition
podcast.body: The band's singer, Sarah Bettens, amassed a large lesbian following during K's Choice's heyday. After moving to Tennessee and working as a firefighter, Sarah transitioned to a man in 2019 and now goes by the name Sam Bettens. He currently resides in Palm Desert, California, with his partner, two stepchildren, and two adopted children. "Then in 2019, Sarah transitioned to a man. And now goes by the name Sam Betons."
